issues.t: Worn ignition switch can cause no-start or stalling (recall)
issues.sym: The car is hard to start for a while, then may suddenly shut off while driving. It usually restarts right away.
issues.why: Electrical contacts inside the ignition switch wear out early. Honda recalled affected cars to replace the switch.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Run your VIN for open recalls and have the switch replaced. Until then, avoid highway driving if it has stalled before.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping and failure
issues.sym: Slipping, flare or harsh shifts, a flashing D or D4 light, and eventually no drive at all.
issues.why: Internal clutch and gear wear in the automatic. Failures are most common on 2001-2004 cars, especially V6 models.
issues.next: Stop driving hard on it once it slips. Have the fluid and codes checked; a slipping unit usually needs a rebuild or replacement.

issues.t: Takata 'Alpha' airbag inflator: do-not-drive warning
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can see or feel. The danger shows up only in a crash, when the inflator can rupture and throw metal fragments.
issues.why: These early Takata inflators degrade with age and heat. Federal safety officials told owners of 2001-2002 Accords to park them until repaired.
issues.next: Do not drive the car until the airbag recall is done. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls; Honda can arrange towing or a mobile repair.

issues.t: Radio and climate-control display goes dim or dark
issues.sym: The radio, clock and climate-control readouts fade or go completely dark, making the controls hard to use at night.
issues.why: The display backlight circuit on the audio/climate unit fails. Honda gave this a longer warranty in the past, but that coverage has run out.
issues.next: A repaired circuit board or replacement audio unit fixes it. Not a safety issue, but the heater and A/C settings become hard to read.

issues.t: V6 oil burning and misfires (cylinder deactivation)
issues.sym: Oil level drops between changes, check engine light for misfire, rough running and fouled spark plugs.
issues.why: Running on fewer cylinders lets oil deposits build on the piston rings, so the rings stick and oil gets into the cylinders. Honda settled a class action and covered piston-ring repairs under an extended warranty.
issues.next: Check oil often and keep records. Have misfire codes diagnosed; ask Honda about any goodwill help for ring repairs.

issues.t: 4-cylinder oil consumption from sticking piston rings
issues.sym: The engine uses oil between changes and the low-oil light may come on. Some cars show a little smoke on start-up.
issues.why: Deposits build on the oil control rings so they stick. Honda extended the piston and ring warranty on these engines (bulletin 12-087).
issues.next: Check the oil level every fill-up and write down how much it uses. Honda's extended warranty for this (bulletin A12-087) lasted 8 years or 125,000 miles from the original sale, so most cars are now outside it, but the bulletin still describes the fix a shop can do.

issues.t: Loud rattle for a few seconds on cold start (VTC actuator)
issues.sym: A loud grinding or rattling noise right after a cold start that goes away within a couple of seconds.
issues.why: The variable valve timing (VTC) actuator on the intake cam rattles until oil pressure builds. Honda issued a service bulletin to replace it.
issues.next: Mention the noise at your next service and ask for the updated VTC actuator. It is usually not urgent, but fix it before the timing chain wears.

issues.t: Rear brake pads wear out early
issues.sym: Squealing or grinding from the rear wheels much sooner than expected.
issues.why: The original rear pad design put too much braking force on the rear wheels. Honda settled a class action and released redesigned pads.
issues.next: Have the rear pads checked at every oil change and use the updated pads when replacing them.

issues.t: Rusted front driveshaft can break (recall)
issues.sym: Clicking or clunking from a front axle, then a sudden loss of power to the wheels. Mostly cars from road-salt states.
issues.why: Road salt can corrode the front driveshafts until they crack. Honda recalled the cars to inspect and replace the driveshafts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the free inspection. If you hear clunking from the front, stop driving and have it towed in.

issues.t: CVT belt slip with engine-speed surge (software update)
issues.sym: Engine RPM suddenly flares at highway speed and the check engine light comes on (code P1890).
issues.why: A wrong learned value in the engine computer can let CVT pressure drop so the belt slips. Honda released a software update.
issues.next: Have a Honda dealer check that the software update was done. If P1890 is already stored, the dealer may need to replace the CVT.

issues.t: Passenger seat weight sensor can crack (airbag recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on, or the passenger airbag on/off indicator may act strangely.
issues.why: The sensor that tells the car if someone is in the front passenger seat can crack and short out. The airbag may then deploy or stay off when it should not.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-332 and, on 2020–2022 models, recall 24V-064, and get the repair done soon. Keep children in the back seat until it is fixed.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking activates for no reason
issues.sym: The car brakes hard on its own with nothing in the way, sometimes with a collision warning on the dash.
issues.why: The collision mitigation braking system can misread the road ahead. Federal safety officials opened an investigation into these Accords.
issues.next: Report every event to a Honda dealer and to NHTSA, and ask about software updates. Leave extra room behind you until it is checked.

issues.t: In-tank fuel pump can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, a check engine light, the engine stalling while driving, or a car that will not start.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump inside the tank can stop working. Honda recalled the cars to replace the pump.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 20V-314 and 21V-215 and get the free pump replacement before driving far.

issues.t: Fuel in the engine oil (oil dilution)
issues.sym: Oil level rises on the dipstick and the oil smells like gasoline, mostly in cold weather and with short trips.
issues.why: On cold starts some fuel washes past the piston rings into the oil. Owners have sued, saying this wears bearings and can lead to engine damage.
issues.next: Check the oil level often, change it on time or sooner, and take longer drives when you can. Ask the dealer about software updates.

issues.t: Stability-control unit can leak brake fluid (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal travels further than normal, or the car may creep when it should be held.
issues.why: A valve inside the stability-control (VSA) modulator can leak brake fluid. Honda recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for recall 23V-430. If the pedal feels long or soft, have the car towed in rather than driven.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A raw gasoline smell, especially after driving, and possibly a check engine light.
issues.why: The engine-mounted high-pressure fuel pump can crack and leak fuel, which is a fire risk. Honda recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park it and have it towed. Check your VIN for recall 24V-763 and get the free repair.

issues.t: Driver seat cushion frame may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: The driver's seat may feel loose, shift or rock when you sit down or brake.
issues.why: Bolts on the seat cushion frame may not have been tightened at the factory, so the seat may not hold you properly in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 24V-859 and 26V-054 and get the free repair soon. Stop driving if the seat moves noticeably.

issues.t: Front seat belt pretensioner may be missing a rivet (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can notice in normal driving.
issues.why: A rivet may be missing from the front seat belt pretensioner, so the belt may not hold the occupant properly in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-782 and get the free inspection and repair soon.

issues.t: Power steering hose can leak onto hot exhaust (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid spots under the front of the car, a whining pump, heavier steering, or smoke and a burning-oil smell from under the hood.
issues.why: On V6 cars the power steering feed hose sits close to hot engine parts. Years of heat can make it brittle so it cracks and leaks fluid, which can smoke or catch fire. Honda recalled these cars to fit an improved hose.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 12V-222 and have the free hose replacement done. If you see smoke or smell burning fluid, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: 12-volt battery sensor can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning. Sometimes a burning smell or smoke from the battery area under the hood, or a battery or charging warning.
issues.why: A small sensor clamped to the negative battery terminal can let in water and road salt. Over time it can short out and overheat. Honda recalled the cars to replace or seal the sensor.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for recall 17V-418 and get the free repair.

issues.t: Starter motor wears out early or grinds
issues.sym: The engine needs several tries of the start button or key before it cranks, or there is a grinding noise as it starts. Eventually it will not crank at all.
issues.why: The starter motor on this generation is a known weak point. Honda also issued a bulletin for 2013-2015 V6 automatic cars with a grinding starter, which calls for a new starter and repositioning the torque converter.
issues.next: Have the battery tested first, since a weak battery causes the same symptom. If the battery is good, plan on a starter replacement before it leaves you stranded.

issues.t: LED daytime running lights burn out
issues.sym: One or both of the LED strips in the headlights go dim, flicker or stop lighting, while the regular headlights still work.
issues.why: The LED running lights are built into the headlight housing and can fail early. Honda extended the warranty on some 2016-2017 cars under bulletin 19-042.
issues.next: Ask a Honda dealer whether your VIN is covered by bulletin 19-042. Outside that coverage the whole headlight unit usually has to be replaced, so it can wait if the main headlights work.

issues.t: Automatic transmission bearing can break (recall)
issues.sym: A grinding or whirring noise that grows with speed, a check engine light, and in bad cases the car can still creep after you shift into Park.
issues.why: Hard driving can crack the outer race of a shaft bearing inside the automatic transmission, and the broken pieces chew up the gear train.
issues.next: Have the recall software update done and the transmission checked for noise now, because a broken bearing can cost you the whole transmission or let the car roll in Park.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture or underinflate (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing shows up day to day. The problem only appears in a crash, when the airbag may burst and throw metal pieces or inflate too weakly.
issues.why: The original driver inflator absorbs moisture over the years, which changes how its propellant burns.
issues.next: Check the VIN and get the free inflator replacement before driving the car again; this one is separate from the later Takata campaigns.

issues.t: Parking pawl may not hold the car in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The car creeps or rolls after you shift into Park on a slope, even though the shifter shows P.
issues.why: A casting flaw in the transmission cover can keep the parking pawl from dropping fully into place.
issues.next: Use the parking brake every time and get the recall repair done, because a car that rolls away can hurt someone.

issues.t: Hybrid system can reset and cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: The car suddenly loses drive power while you are moving, with hybrid system and other warnings on the dash. It often drives again after a restart.
issues.why: A software fault makes the hybrid control unit reset itself, which drops the motors out of drive.
issues.next: Get the recall software update now, since losing power in traffic or on a highway merge is dangerous.

issues.t: Tire repair kit sealant bottle cap can come off (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing until you need the kit, then the bottle may spray sealant or the cap may blow off when you connect it.
issues.why: Pressure can build inside the sealant bottle and push the cap loose, so the kit may not seal the tire.
issues.next: Have the kit replaced under the recall and carry another plan for a flat in the meantime; these cars have no spare tire.

issues.t: Front seat belt buckle may not latch (recall 23V-158)
issues.sym: A front seat belt won't click into its buckle, or won't stay latched when you tug it.
issues.why: On some 2018–2019 Accords, part of the front seat belt buckle can block the latch, so the belt won't latch. A belt that isn't latched can't protect you in a crash (recall 23V-158).
issues.next: Make sure each front belt clicks and holds when you tug it. If one won't latch, don't let anyone ride in that seat until it is fixed. Check your VIN for recall 23V-158.

issues.t: Wipers, lights or camera can stop working from a software fault (recall 20V-771)
issues.sym: The wipers, defroster, rearview camera, outside lights, power windows or warning chimes stop working, on and off or for good.
issues.why: On some 2018–2020 Accords, a software error in the body control module can cut communication with other parts, so the wipers, defroster, rearview camera, exterior lights and other features can stop working (recall 20V-771).
issues.next: If the wipers, defroster or lights quit while you're driving, slow down and pull over where it's safe; restarting the car may bring them back. Check your VIN for recall 20V-771 and get the software update.

issues.t: Overheating or coolant loss from head gasket (warranty extension)
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, coolant keeps going down with no puddle, or the engine shakes and the check engine light comes on (often codes P0300–P0304).
issues.why: On some Accords the head gasket can let coolant into the engine. Honda extended the warranty on this part to 10 years or 150,000 miles from the original purchase date for: 2018–2022 1.5L turbo with CVT (bulletin 26-003), 2018–2020 1.5L turbo with manual transmission (26-004), 2018–2022 Accord Hybrid (26-006) and 2023–2026 Accord Hybrid (26-007).
issues.next: If the temperature gauge goes into the red or steam appears, pull over when it is safe, turn the engine off and don't open the radiator cap while hot. Don't keep driving an overheating engine. Ask a Honda dealer to check your VIN for bulletins 26-003, 26-004, 26-006 or 26-007; if it qualifies, the repair may be covered under the extended warranty.
